rationale: The candidate reads as a single coherent terraced-bent mass across all four views, so it clears the one-view / collision rejection. The dominant gesture is legible and the hierarchy is strong: a compact stepped base rising into a bent upper cap. The main weakness is programmatic publicness at the verified access edge: the blue frontage is not translated into a clearly active court, undercut, or seam, so the ground response feels more sealed than spatially engaged. Still, the form remains plausible for neighborhood living / mixed-use because it supports a compact capacity-aware mass with some upper articulation and does not collapse into a purely decorative object. The silhouette is coherent but the stepping is somewhat generic rather than exceptional as inhabitable section, hence a mid score rather than a top one. Reference 1 strongly resonates in dominant-prism clarity; reference 3 supports the idea of carved public openness but is more landscape-rich than this candidate; reference 4 offers base/upper hierarchy but is tower-like and only partial; reference 5 is counterfactual and useful only as an operation cue for a stronger public seam, not as a form model.
